일곱.forms: native · counting things, hours, age · same before a counter (일곱 개, 일곱 시)
일곱.x: I get up at seven in the morning.
일곱.e: Not related to Sino-Korean 일 (one) — 일곱 is seven. 일곱 시 = 7 o'clock.

새벽.m: dawn, early morning (the hours after midnight)
새벽.x: I went to bed at 2 a.m. last night.
새벽.t: 새벽 covers roughly midnight to sunrise: 새벽 한 시 = 1 a.m.

구경하다.m: to look around, to sightsee, to watch (for fun)
구경하다.x: I looked around Myeongdong on the weekend.
구경하다.e: Watching for fun — sightseeing, window shopping; 구경꾼 = onlooker.
구경하다.t: In shops, 그냥 구경하고 있어요 = 'I'm just looking.'

월급.x: When I get paid, I save a little.

관광지.ex: 경주는 오래된 절이 많은 관광지로 유명해요.
관광지.x: Gyeongju is famous as a tourist spot with many old temples.

예약.ex: 인기 있는 식당이라서 일주일 전에 예약을 했어요.
예약.x: It's a popular restaurant, so I made a reservation a week ahead.
예약.t: For tickets (movies, trains), Koreans usually say 예매; for tables and rooms, 예약.

설명하다.ex: 이 단어의 뜻을 다시 설명해 주세요.
설명하다.x: Please explain the meaning of this word again.
설명하다.t: 설명해 주세요 is the go-to way to ask a teacher to explain something.

전화를 받다.forms: 전화를 받아요 · 받았어요 · 받을 거예요 · 받으세요
전화를 받다.m: to answer the phone, to take a call
전화를 받다.ex: 수업 중이라서 전화를 받을 수 없었어요.
전화를 받다.x: I was in class, so I couldn't answer the phone.
전화를 받다.e: 받다 means 'to receive': you receive the call.
전화를 받다.t: When you answer, say 여보세요; to hang up is 전화를 끊다.

밟다.m: to step on, to tread on
밟다.x: I stepped on someone's foot on the subway.
밟다.t: Pronounced [밥따], but 밟아요 is [발바요] — the ㄹ comes back before vowels.

신청서.x: Fill out this application form and hand it in at the window.

신용 카드.x: I didn't have cash, so I paid by credit card.
신용 카드.t: Cashiers may ask 일시불로 해 드릴까요? — pay in full, as opposed to 할부, installments.

태양.ex: 태양에서 나오는 에너지로 전기를 만들 수 있어요.
태양.x: We can make electricity with energy from the sun.
태양.e: Literally 'the great yang' — the ultimate source of light and warmth.
태양.t: In daily talk Koreans say 해; 태양 sounds scientific or poetic.

반응하다.x: The baby reacted right away to its mom's voice.
반응하다.t: 반응하다 is a natural reaction; 대응하다 is deliberately dealing with a problem.

민족.x: Lunar New Year is a big holiday for the Korean people.
민족.t: Koreans often say 우리 민족 'our people' to mean all ethnic Koreans, across both Koreas.

구직.x: I started job hunting after graduation.
구직.t: Contrast: 구인 is the company seeking workers.

절약.ex: 에너지 절약을 위해서 안 쓰는 불은 꺼 주세요.
절약.x: To save energy, please turn off lights you aren't using.
절약.t: Pronounced [저략]: the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.

취업난.x: Young people are having a harder and harder time finding jobs.
취업난.e: Literally 'job-getting difficulty'; -난 = shortage or crisis: 취업난, 주택난.
취업난.t: Pronounced [취엄난] — ㅂ becomes ㅁ before ㄴ.

유통.x: If you cut down the distribution process, prices go down.
유통.e: Literally 'flowing through' — goods moving from maker to shop.
유통.t: 유통 기한 (sell-by date) is the version you'll see on every food package.

실종되다.x: A man who went hiking went missing in the mountains.
실종되다.t: Pronounced [실쫑되다]; 실종 신고 = a missing-person report.

진학.m: going on to the next level of school (e.g. college)
진학.x: He's thinking about going on to grad school.

무용.ex: 그녀는 어릴 때부터 한국 무용을 배웠어요.
무용.x: She has learned Korean dance since she was little.
무용.t: 무용 is formal or artistic dance; everyday dancing is 춤: 춤을 추다.

촬영.x: This drama was filmed in Busan.
촬영.t: Signs saying 촬영 금지 mean 'No photography'.

및.ex: 자세한 일정 및 장소는 홈페이지에서 확인하세요.
및.x: Check the homepage for the detailed schedule and location.
및.e: Probably from old 및다 'to reach', the root of today's 미치다 'to reach'.
및.t: Only links nouns in formal writing such as notices and reports; never say it in casual conversation.

감당하다.m: to handle, to cope with, to bear
감당하다.ex: 혼자서 그 많은 일을 감당하기 어려워요.
감당하다.x: It's hard to handle all that work alone.
감당하다.t: Often negative: 감당할 수 없다 / 감당이 안 되다 'it's too much for me'.
rel: to be too much to handle

옥탑방.x: Rooftop rooms are hot in summer and cold in winter.
옥탑방.e: Literally 'room in the rooftop structure' — a small unit built on a building's roof.

천만다행.m: a great stroke of luck, a huge relief; thank goodness
천만다행.ex: 큰 사고였는데 아무도 안 다쳐서 천만다행이에요.
천만다행.x: It was a big accident, but thank goodness nobody got hurt.
천만다행.e: 千萬 'ten million' + 多幸 'good fortune' — lucky ten million times over.
천만다행.t: A stronger 다행이다; said after a near miss. 불행 중 다행 means 'a blessing in disguise / it could have been worse'.

비장하다.m: grim but heroic, solemn and determined
비장하다.x: The players entered the final with grim determination.

세속.m: the secular world, worldly life; common custom
세속.ex: 그는 세속의 욕심을 버리고 산으로 들어갔어요.
세속.x: He gave up worldly desires and went into the mountains.
세속.e: Literally 'the world and its customs', as opposed to religious life.

번아웃.ex: 야근이 계속되면서 번아웃이 와서 휴가를 냈어요.
번아웃.x: With the constant overtime, I burned out and took a vacation.
번아웃.e: From English 'burnout'; the formal medical term is 탈진 증후군.
번아웃.t: Common collocations: 번아웃이 오다 (burnout hits) and 번아웃에 빠지다 (to fall into burnout).

기록물.x: These records were inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.
기록물.e: Literally 'recorded things'. -물 = thing or material: 건축물, 인쇄물.
기록물.t: Pronounced [기롱물] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ.

전통문화.ex: 외국인 관광객들은 한국의 전통문화에 관심이 많아요.
전통문화.x: Foreign tourists are very interested in traditional Korean culture.

야속하다.m: to be hurtfully cold, unkind (making you feel let down)
야속하다.x: I felt a little hurt that my friend forgot my birthday.
야속하다.e: Hanja mean 'rustic, vulgar'; today it means feeling hurt by someone's coldness.
야속하다.t: Pronounced [야소카다]; also for things like 야속한 세월 — time that cruelly flies.

생물다양성.x: When forests disappear, biodiversity also decreases.

마당놀이.m: madangnori, open-air folk theater performed in the round
마당놀이.ex: 연말이 되면 부모님과 함께 마당놀이를 보러 가요.
마당놀이.x: At the end of the year, I go see madangnori with my parents.
마당놀이.e: 마당 'yard' + 놀이 'play': staged in an open space with the audience all around.
마당놀이.t: Audience participation is expected: laughing, shouting back and even joining in are part of the show.

미세플라스틱.x: Microplastics were even found in fish caught in the sea.

조력.ex: 시화호에는 세계적인 규모의 조력 발전소가 있습니다.
조력.x: Sihwa Lake has a world-class tidal power plant.
조력.t: Homonym: 조력 (助力) also means 'help, assistance'; 조력자 is 'helper'.

준용하다.m: to apply mutatis mutandis, to apply correspondingly (law or rule)
준용하다.x: We apply this regulation correspondingly to contract employees as well.
준용하다.e: Literally 'use by analogy' — applying a rule to a similar case.
준용하다.t: A legal-document word: you'll see it as '제○조를 준용한다' in statutes.

진력하다.m: to do one's utmost, to devote all one's energy
진력하다.x: The government said it would do its utmost to recover from the damage.
진력하다.e: Literally 'exhaust one's strength' — giving everything to a task.
진력하다.t: Pronounced [질려카다] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

머쓱하다.ex: 인사를 했는데 아무도 대답을 안 해서 머쓱했어요.
머쓱하다.x: I said hello but nobody answered, so I felt awkward.
머쓱하다.t: Pronounced [머쓰카다]; often in 머쓱하게 웃다 'to laugh sheepishly'.
